# Keep the Superseded Version in Tree

When something is replaced, the replaced thing is not deleted. It stays beside its successor.
Confirmed in seven repositories, in four distinct motives — which is what makes it a pattern rather
than untidiness.

## Motive 1 — pedagogical, on purpose

`Oracle-Database-Laboratories` keeps a three-trigger-plus-package-state implementation next to the
compound trigger that replaced it, and labels the loser:

> "This works, but it is fragile in a way worth naming ... The guard flag below is what stops that
> recursion. Version (b) has no such problem and is the one to prefer."
> — Oracle-Database-Laboratories/sql/03_plsql/04_triggers.sql, 2026-07-25

Same instinct in `Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence`: `docs/lab-1-notes.txt` and
`lab-2-notes.txt` hold the **as-submitted** coursework SQL, bugs and all, while `sql/01_analytics/`
rewrites each query with a comment explaining what was wrong. A before/after record, deliberately
kept. See [[multiple-solutions-side-by-side]] for the same habit applied to alternatives that are all
correct.

## Motive 2 — a generated artefact with its pristine source

`IT Applications in Business and Commerce` keeps `chapters.backup.js` (454 lines, hand-written)
beside the generated `chapters.js` (567 lines, `DO-NOT-EDIT` banner, deterministic seed 1337). The
"backup" is in fact the source of truth. Covered on
[[generated-artifact-with-pristine-source]].

## Motive 3 — the rejected design, still shipped

`Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence` argues at length that a technical indicator must be a
measure, not a dimension — and then ships `project/twtr/ssas/Dim RSI.dim` with `RSIKey`,
`IsOverbought`, `IsOversold` attributes, i.e. exactly the rejected model. The SQL side ships the
winner; the SSAS side ships the loser. See [[rsi-as-measure-not-dimension]].

## Motive 4 — inertia, and it costs something

- `Information-Systems-Modelling` carries a **39-file nested duplicate** Angular project — the
  pre-rewrite student-CRUD scaffold — inside the real app, plus a 557-line `instances.ttl` referenced
  by no code, README or pom, plus two byte-identical copies of `ontology.ttl` in different labs.
- `IT Applications in Business and Commerce` keeps two complete `gym_torcs/` trees with
  `snakeoil3_gym.py` (605 lines) duplicated between them, upstream leftovers neither agent uses, and
  a `commands.txt` that is an exact stale copy naming the wrong checkpoint files.
- `labour-fraud-analysis` wrote `build_viewer.py::strip_locale()` to remove a second locale, and
  `interactive/i18n.js` still advertises "i18n (EN / PL)" while `app.js` still branches on `'pl'`.
- `browser_game_stickfps/files/` holds pristine 2026-07-14 seed copies of `TASKS.md`, an empty
  `PROGRESS.md` skeleton and the four agent files — a bootstrap kit left in place.

## The instructive counter-example

`Information-Systems-Modelling` `98fac45 refactor(lab6): drop hand-written snapshot pages, generate
from the app` **deleted** six hand-written HTML pages, −1268 lines. It is the only place in the whole
source set where a superseded version was removed rather than kept — and it is also the only commit
in that repo that reads like a working log rather than an import. See
[[generate-markup-instead-of-hand-writing-it]].

## Why it matters for retrieval

A reader cannot tell motive 1 from motive 4 by looking at the tree. Both leave two versions side by
side. The distinguishing evidence is whether a comment names the loser as inferior — which is the
same discipline as [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]]. Where no such comment exists, this wiki
treats the duplicate as inertia and says so.
